text: It is one of the most difficult things in the world to look at anything simply.
author: Jiddu Krishnamurti

text: Life is an experimental journey undertaken involuntarily.
author: Fernando Pessoa

text: Interest is the most important thing in life; happiness is temporary, but interest is continuous.
author: Georgia O’Keeffe

text: Don't get bored with peace. Be in it. Go deeper into it. Look between the thoughts.
author: Nisargadatta Maharaj

text: When we are no longer able to change a situation, we are challenged to change ourselves.
author: Victor Frankl

text: Not knowing how near the truth is, people seek it far away.
author: Hakuin Ekaku

text: One can acquire certainty only by amputating inquiry.
author: Marvin Minsky

text: One can be the master of what one does, but never of what one feels.
author: Gustave Flaubert

author: BeautyOfSaas

text: I learned more from idiots and nobodies than from professors of this and that. Life is the teacher, not the Board of Education.

author: Michael Moritz

text: I look at what I have not and think myself unhappy; others look at what I have and think me happy.
author: Joseph Roux

text: Beyond a wholesome discipline, be gentle with yourself. You are a child of the universe no less than the trees and the stars; you have a right to be here.
author: Max Ehrmann

text: Worry often gives a small thing a big shadow.
author: Swedish proverb

text: The illusion of speed is the belief that it saves time. But haste and speed accelerate time, which passes more quickly, and two hours of hurry shorten a day.
author: Frédéric Gros

text: A moment of self-compassion can change your entire day. A string of such moments can change the course of your life.
author: Christopher Germer

text: The worst lesson that can be taught to a man is to rely upon others and to whine over his sufferings.
author: Teddy Roosevelt

author: Georgia O'Keeffe

text: Until we understand the assumptions in which we are drenched we cannot know ourselves.
author: Adrienne Rich

text: I don't say we all ought to misbehave, but we ought to look as if we could.
author: Orson Welles

text: Who is initiating the items on your to-do list? When I'm most productive, I decide what I want to create and work on the task that will help build my vision. When I am less productive, I spend my day responding to what someone else sends to me — emails, texts, etc. — and often that means I end up building someone else's vision.
author: James Clear

text: A real diamond, his father used to say, is never entirely free of inclusions. A real diamond is never perfect.
author: Anthony Doerr

text: Just set one day’s work in front of the last day’s work. That’s the way it comes out. And that’s the only way it does.
author: John Steinbeck

text: It is utterly false and cruelly arbitrary to put all the play and learning into childhood, all the work into middle age, and all the regrets into old age.
author: Margaret Mead

text: Many paths lead from the foot of the mountain, but at the peak we all gaze at the single bright moon.
author: Ikkyu

text: It is amazing what you can accomplish if you do not care who gets the credit.
author: Harry S. Truman

text: He who makes no mistakes makes no progress.
author: Teddy Roosevelt

text: My life amounts to no more than one drop in a limitless ocean. Yet what is any ocean, but a multitude of drops?
author: David Mitchell

text: To a very great degree, school is a place where children learn to be stupid.
author: John Holt

text: In most of our human relationships, we spend much of our time reassuring one another that our costumes of identity are on straight.
author: Ram Dass

text: Delaying a conversation doesn't make it easier.
author: James Clear

text: You are not your grand plans. You are your daily patterns.
author: James Clear

text: You are what you do, not what you say you'll do.
author: Carl Jung

text: I learned to always take on things I'd never done before. Growth and comfort do not coexist.
author: Ginni Rometty

text: It is better to solve one problem five different ways, than to solve five problems one way.
author: George Pólya

text: Paths are made by walking.
author: Franz Kafka

text: The truth does not change based on our ability to stomach it.
author: Flannery o'Connor

text: I think the notion of retirement is just a dreadful, dreadful idea and I hope I never have to do that.
author: Michael Moritz

text: All happy families are alike; each unhappy family is unhappy in its own way.
author: Leo Tolstoy

text: Always remember that you are absolutely unique. Just like everyone else.
author: Margaret Mead

text: Someone I loved once gave me a box full of darkness. It took me years to understand that this, too, was a gift.
author: Mary Oliver

text: Character consists of what you do on the third and fourth tries.
author: James Michener

text: The most important point is to accept yourself and to stand on your two feet.
author: Shunryu Suzuki

text: The maxim 'Nothing avails but perfection' may be spelt shorter: 'Paralysis.'
author: Winston Churchill

text: Do not be angry with the rain; it simply does not know how to fall upwards.
author: Vladimir Nabokov

text: You have to do nothing to be who you are. Nothing at all.
author: H. W. L. Poonja

text: The surest sign of wisdom is continual cheerfulness.
author: Michel de Montaigne

text: Fear is a manipulative emotion that can trick us into living a boring life.
author: Donald Miller

text: Fear and ego—in other words, ignorance—are keeping your hand on the tiller. Release the tiller for whatever reason, and the steering takes care of itself.
author: Jed McKenna

text: When one tugs at a single thing in nature, he finds it attached to the rest of the world.
author: John Muir

text: Learning is a weightless treasure you can always carry easily.
author: Chinese Proverb

text: Awe is the moment when ego surrenders to wonder.
author: Terry Tempest Williams

text: Happiness as a goal is a recipe for disaster.
author: Barry Schwartz

text: What am I doing? Nothing. I am letting life rain upon me.
author: Rahel Varnhagen

text: It's one thing to get what you want. But it's another thing to want what's worth getting.
author: Shane Parrish

text: I am not a thing in the world; I am the space in which the world is happening.
author: Richard Lang

text: Patience is a form of wisdom. It demonstrates that we understand and accept the fact that sometimes things must unfold in their own time.
author: Jon Kabat-Zinn

text: If I know what I shall find, I do not want to find it. Uncertainty is the salt of life.
author: Erwin Chargaff

text: The homemaker has the ultimate career. All other careers exist for one purpose only - and that is to support the ultimate career.
author: C. S. Lewis

text: Don't you want to be alive before you die?
author: Anthony Doerr

text: Dying societies accumulate laws like dying men accumulate remedies.
author: Nicolás Gómez Dávila

text: Wisdom is oftentimes nearer when we stoop than when we soar.
author: William Wordsworth

text: I have learned silence from the talkative, toleration from the intolerant, and kindness from the unkind; yet strange, I am ungrateful to these teachers.
author: Kahlil Gibran

text: You can’t define a person. You can’t sum anyone up. Life is non-summative—it is infinite.
author: James Low

text: Rudeness is the weak man’s imitation of strength.
author: Eric Hoffer

text: The creative adult is the child who survived.
author: Julian F. Fleron

text: No emotion, any more than a wave, can long retain its own individual form.
author: Henry Ward Beecher

text: He who jumps into the void owes no explanation to those who stand and watch.
author: Jean-Luc Godard

text: Hope for forces which you do not yet have. That is what is most impossible, and nevertheless possible.
author: Rahel Varnhagen

text: You can cut all the flowers but you cannot keep spring from coming.
author: Pablo Neruda

author: Ann Patchett

text: Love is the quality of attention we pay to things.
author: J. D. McClatchy

text: The truth is not a crystal that can be slipped into one's pocket, but an endless current into which one falls headlong.
author: Robert Musil

text: If you are lonely when you are alone, you are in bad company.
author: Jean-Paul Sartre

text: We choose to do these things, not because they are easy, but because they are hard.
author: John F. Kennedy

text: Not till we are lost, in other words not till we have lost the world, do we begin to find ourselves, and realize where we are and the infinite extent of our relations.
author: Henry David Thoreau

text: Calm down. Both your sins and your good deeds will be lost in oblivion.
author: Czesław Miłosz

text: In my whole life, I have known no wise people (over a broad subject matter area) who didn’t read all the time—none, zero.
author: Charlie Munger

text: Now, there is a law written in the darkest of the Books of Life, and it is this: If you look at a thing nine hundred and ninety-nine times, you are perfectly safe; if you look at it the thousandth time, you are in frightful danger of seeing it for the first time.
author: G.K. Chesterton

text:
The sense of danger must not disappear:
The way is certainly both short and steep,
However gradual it looks from here;
Look if you like, but you will have to leap.
author: W.H. Auden

text: The point of modern propaganda isn't only to misinform or push an agenda. It is to exhaust your critical thinking, to annihilate truth.
author: Garry Kasparov

text: In times of change, learners inherit the earth, while the learned find themselves beautifully equipped to deal with a world that no longer exists.
author: Eric Hoffer

text: Do everything with a mind that lets go. Do not expect praise or reward.
author: Ajahn Chah

text: There is nothing more important to true growth than realizing that you are not the voice of the mind, you are the one who hears it.
author: Michael A. Singer

text: When people reveal themselves, believe them. Stop painting prettier pictures with the red flags you see.
author: Morgan Richard Olivier

text: There are three musts that hold us back: I must do well. You must treat me well. And the world must be easy.
author: Albert Ellis

text: What you seek is seeking you.
author: Rumi

text: To pay attention, this is our endless and proper work.
author: Mary Oliver

text: A country is not only what it does but what it tolerates.
author: Kurt Tucholsky

text: Life is a process of becoming, a combination of states we have to go through. Where people fail is that they wish to elect a state and remain in it. This is a kind of death.
author: Anaïs Nin

text: Nobody ever figures out what life is all about, and it doesn't matter. Explore the world. Nearly everything is really interesting if you go into it deeply enough.
author: Richard Feynman

text: At some point in life the world's beauty becomes enough. You don't need to photograph, paint or even remember it. It is enough.
author: Toni Morrison

text: In the depth of winter, I finally learned that within me there lay an invincible summer.
author: Albert Camus

text: See how letting go of the world is peaceful. There's nothing you need to hold on to. There's nothing you need to push away.
author: Buddha

text: It doesn't matter if the water is cold or warm if you're going to have to wade through it anyway.
author: Pierre Teilhard de Chardin

text: To inhabit silence in our oneness is to stop telling the story altogether.
author: David Whyte

text: The first effect of adjusting to other people is that one becomes boring.
author: Elias Canetti

text: The world won't come to me… so I must go to it.
author: Donna Tartt

text: Salute the audience.
author: Patrick Winston

text: Change will lead to insight far more often than insight will lead to change.
author: Milton Erickson

text:
Trust follows consistency.

The business that delivers a quality product every time earns the customer's trust.

The person in the relationship who shows up reliably — who keeps promises, who responds with steadiness — earns the trust of the other.

The pattern is the proof."
author: James Clear

text: The urge to save humanity is almost always only a false-face for the urge to rule it.
author: H. L. Mencken

text: The real truth, that dare not speak itself, is that no one is in control. Absolutely no one.
author: Terence Mckenna

text: The power of imagination makes us infinite.
author: John Muir

text: If you stay still, earth buries you, ready or not.
author: Annie Dillard

text: No faith that is not surrounded by doubt can survive.
author: Elias Canetti

text: Do not wish for an easy life. Wish for the strength to endure a difficult one.
author: Bruce Lee

text: Foolishness is a twin sister of wisdom.

text: The years teach much which the days never know.
author: Ralph Waldo Emerson

text: It's not where you take things from — it's where you take things to.
author: Jean-Luc Godard

text: The eyes see only what the mind is prepared to comprehend.
author: Henri Bergson

text: Timidity can be as dangerous as rashness.

text: The miracle is not to walk on water. The miracle is to walk on the green earth in the present moment, to appreciate the peace and beauty that are available now.

text: Simplicity and inner calm are more important than complexity and superficial agitation in architecture.
author: Christopher Alexander

text: Coming back to where you started is not the same as never leaving.

text: If you want to be a good thinker, you must develop a mind that can jump the jurisdictional boundaries. You don't have to know it all. Just take in the best big ideas from all these disciplines. And it's not that hard to do.
author: Charlie Munger

text: Learning happens when someone wants to learn, not when someone wants to teach.
author: Roger Schank

text: Where I was born and where and how I have lived is unimportant. It is what I have done with where I have been that should be of interest.
author: Georgia O’Keeffe

text: A pessimist sees the difficulty in every opportunity; an optimist sees the opportunity in every difficulty.
author: Winston Churchill

text: Part of what is happening when you spend 7 hours reading a book, is you spend 7 hours with your mind on the topics in the book, grappling with them, drawing connections, having thoughts you would not otherwise have had. And so without that process of grappling, without those hours inside that book, it doesn't get inside you. It doesn't impress itself upon you. It doesn't change you. text: Fear, to a great extent, is born of a story we tell ourselves.

text: You can't test courage cautiously.

author: Marvin Minsky

text: Enlightenment is always preceded by confusion.

author: André Gide

text: The language in which we express our ideas has a strong influence on our thought processes.
author: Donald Knuth

text: You sense far more than you are conscious of. Whether you want to or not.
author: Tor Nørretranders

text: Silence, I discover, is something you can actually hear.
author: Haruki Murakami

text: In wisdom gathered over time I have found that every experience is a form of exploration.
author: Aldous Huxley

text: In the space between chaos and shape there was another chance.

author: George Berkeley

author: Henry Miller

text: You aren't wealthy until you have something money can't buy.

text: It doesn't matter what others do, unless you decide that it matters to you.
author: Michael A. Singer

text: The mind is not a vessel to be filled, but a fire to be kindled.
author: Plutarch

text: No unforced errors.
author: Unknown

text: If intelligence is getting what you want, wisdom is wanting what's worth getting in the first place.
author: Shane Parrish

text: To live, we must die every instant. We must perish again and again in the storms that make life possible.
author: Thich Nhat Hanh

author: Paul Erdős

text: The only zen you can find on the tops of the mountains is the zen you bring up there.
author: Robert M. Pirsig

author: Frank Crane

author: Albert Ellis

text: There's nothing you can cling to. No refuge. Just let go, man.
author: Alan Watts

text: The unexamined life is not worth living.
author: Socrates

text: The real art of conversation is not only to say the right thing, in the right place, but, far more difficult still, to leave unsaid the wrong thing at the tempting moment.
author: Dorothy Nevill

text: There are many things that seem impossible only so long as one does not attempt them.
author: André Gide

text: Without context, words and actions have no meaning at all.
author: Gregory Bateson

text: We are most of us governed by epistemologies that we know to be wrong.
author: Gregory Bateson

text: Be able to be alone. Lose not the advantage of solitude, and the society of thyself.
author: Thomas Browne

text: Your mind is a compass. Wherever your mind goes, your actions or reactions will ultimately take you.
author: Morgan Richard Olivier

text: The universe is wider than our views of it.
author: Henry David Thoreau

text:
Out of the night that covers me,
Black as the pit from pole to pole,
I thank whatever gods may be
For my unconquerable soul.

In the fell clutch of circumstance
I have not winced nor cried aloud.
Under the bludgeonings of chance
My head is bloody, but unbowed.

Beyond this place of wrath and tears
Looms but the Horror of the shade,
And yet the menace of the years
Finds and shall find me unafraid.

It matters not how strait the gate,
How charged with punishments the scroll,
I am the master of my fate,
I am the captain of my soul.
author: William Ernest Henley

text: It is easier to fight for one’s principles than to live up to them.
author: Alfred Adler

text: Life changes in the instant. The ordinary instant.
author: Joan Didion

text: Be an encourager. The world has plenty of critics already.
author: Dave Willis

text: The surest sign of wisdom is continual cheerfulness.
author: Michel de Montaigne

text: The curious are provided with much fun and wisdom long after formal education has ended.
author: Charlie Munger

text: The aim of life is to live, and to live means to be aware, joyously, drunkenly, serenely, divinely aware.
author: Henry Miller

text: Follow your heart but take your brain with you.
author: Alfred Adler

text: Errors using inadequate data are much less than those using no data at all.
author: Charles Babbage

text: And now that you don't have to be perfect, you can be good.
author: John Steinbeck

text: It’s no use going back to yesterday, because I was a different person then.
author: Lewis Carroll

text: There is only this. Nothing added, nothing missing, nothing left out. What a miracle!
author: Stephan Bodian

text: Figuring out what you don't know or aren't sure of is the greatest intellectual skill of all.
author: John Holt

text: Humans are divided between those who can still look through the eyes of youth and those who cannot.
author: Dave Eggers

text: If you do follow your bliss, you put yourself on a kind of track that has been there all the while, waiting for you, and the life that you ought to be living is the one you are living. When you can see that, you begin to meet people who are in your field of bliss, and they open doors to you. I say: follow your bliss and don't be afraid, and doors will open where you didn't know they were going to be.
author: Joseph Campbell

text: Whatever inspiration is, it’s born from a continuous "I don’t know."
author: Wisława Szymborska

text: Ninety percent of adults spend half their waking lives doing things they would rather not be doing at places they would rather not be.
author: Barry Schwartz

text: No matter how far you have gone down a wrong road, turn back.
author: Turkish proverb

text: The advantage of wisdom is that you can play dumb. The opposite is more difficult.
author: Kurt Tucholsky

text: Three things in human life are important: the first is to be kind; the second is to be kind; and the third is to be kind.
author: Henry James

text: There are no failures - only feedback.
author: Richard Bandler

text: Dictatorships must be feared to survive so they cannot bear to be mocked.
author: Garry Kasparov

text: We have first raised a dust and then complain we cannot see.
author: George Berkeley

text: For both ruin and recovery are from within.
author: Epictetus

text: A fanatic's willingness to kill or be killed in the service of a cause cannot prove the rightness of that cause.
author: Poul Anderson

text: We have to continually be jumping off cliffs and developing our wings on the way down.
author: Kurt Vonnegut

text: We are like butterflies who flutter for a day and think it is forever.
author: Carl Sagan

text: You cannot stay on the summit forever; you have to come down again. So why bother in the first place ? Just this: what is above knows what is below, but what is below dos not know what is above. One climbs, one sees. One descends, one see no longer, but one has seen. There is an art of conducting ourselves in the lower regions by the memory of what one saw higher up. When one can no longer see, one can at least still know.
author: Rene Daumal

text: What we plant in the soil of contemplation, we shall reap in the harvest of action.
author: Meister Eckhart

text: Being curious and excited can take you far, especially over the long arc of a life. The person who is a voracious lifelong learner will figure it out eventually. A strong reader with a healthy dose of curiosity and a willingness to try things is hard to stop.
author: James Clear

text: Without courage, wisdom bears no fruit.
author: Baltasar Gracián

text: Progress isn't made by early risers. It's made by lazy men trying to find easier ways to do something.
author: Robert Heinlein

text: Do you think I count the days ? There is only one day left, always starting over. It is given to us at dawn and taken away from us at dusk.
author: Jean-Paul Sartre

text: What you say about yourself is forgotten. What you do for others compounds. Serve people well, and their word about you will travel further than yours ever could.
author: Shane Parrish

text: How often in life we complete a task that was beyond the capability of the person who we were when we started it.
author: Robert Brault

text: If you want to ruin your life, spend it trying to change your spouse's behaviour.
author: Charlie Munger

text: Nothing diminishes anxiety faster than action.
author: Walter Anderson

text: The goal of life is to be excited to go to work and excited to go home.
author: Josh Kushner

text: Greatness is overrated. It's a form of extremism, and it comes with extreme vices that I have no interest in.
author: Kevin Kelly

text:
The modern world is optimized for convenience, not improvement.

The default path is usually the more convenient path. And I get it. Who wants their days to be a pain in the neck? I like sitting in air-conditioned rooms and watching my favorite shows too.

But the body and mind only grow when placed under a stimulus. If you want improvement, you have to choose something different than convenience.

It can be lovely to have a day where you do not push yourself, but it rarely works out well if you have a life where you do not push yourself.
author: James Clear

text: To sit quietly, without trying to make something special happen, is the most important thing we can do for the transformation of our consciousness.
author: Alan Watts

text: As you think, so shall you become.
author: Bruce Lee

text: At each increase of knowledge, as well as on the contrivance of every new tool, human labour becomes abridged.
author: Charles Babbage

text: So much has been given to me I have not the time to ponder that which has been denied.
author: Helen Keller

text: Almost everything will work again if you unplug it for a few minutes, including you.
author: Anne Lamott

text: To understand and be understood, those are among life's greatest gifts, and every interaction is an opportunity to exchange them.
author: Maria Popova

text: It is the truth that liberates, not your effort to be free.
author: Jiddu Krishnamurti

text: Whether a thought is spoken or not, it is a real thing and has powers of reality.
author: Frank Herbert

text: Premature optimization is the root of all evil.
author: Donald Knuth

text: Making something beautiful is not a new thing or an old thing. It is a constant thing.
author: Christopher Alexander

text: No amount of anxiety makes any difference to anything that is going to happen.
author: Alan Watts

text: It will not be a world of man versus machine. It will be a world of man plus machines.
author: Ginni Rometty

text: People who get an unusual amount of work done are maniacal about removing things from their lives that others tolerate.
author: Shane Parrish

text: It's easier to ask forgiveness than ask permission.
author: Grace Hopper

text: Be patient toward all that is unsolved in your heart and try to love the questions themselves.
author: Rainer Maria Rilke

text: Distrust all in whom the impulse to punish is powerful.
author: Friedrich Nietzsche

text: Discoveries, like resources, may well be infinite: the more we discover, the more we are able to discover.
author: Julian Simon

text: The only way to make sense out of change is to plunge into it, move with it, and join the dance.
author: Alan Watts

text: To enjoy life, the adventurous state of mind must be grasped and maintained. The essential feature of adventure is that it is a going forward into unknown territory.
author: Agnes Martin

text: The Universe began when Nothing saw itself in the mirror.
author: Tor Nørretranders

text: Most people self-limit their ability to learn. Just read books and talk to people. I didn't study rocket engineering, I picked it up along the way.
author: Elon Musk

text: Beware the barrenness of a busy life.
author: Socrates

text: If your eyes are blinded with your worries, you cannot see the beauty of the sunset.
author: Jiddu Krishnamurti

text: The human mind is so constructed that it cannot begin to understand the new until it has done everything in its power to relate it to the old.
author: Henri Bergson

text: In the end, just three things matter: How well we have lived. How well we have loved. How well we have learned to let go.
author: Jack Kornfield

text: And what importance do I have in the courtroom of oblivion?
author: Pablo Neruda

text: Flowers fall even though we love them, and weeds grow even though we dislike them.
author: Dōgen Zenji

text: Live the questions now. Perhaps you will then gradually, without noticing it, live along some distant day into the answer.
author: Rainer Maria Rilke

text: He who has a why to live can bear almost any how.
author: Friedrich Nietzsche

text: Man is profoundly dependent on the reflection of himself in another man's soul, be it even the soul of an idiot.
author: Witold Gombrowicz

text: The effort to try and feel happy is often precisely the thing that makes us miserable.
author: Oliver Burkeman

text: A good life is one in which things do not go perfectly, but you find a way to have a good day regardless.
author: James Clear

text: Always listen to experts. They'll tell you what can't be done, and why. Then do it.
author: Robert Heinlein

text: Wisdom tends to grow in proportion to one's awareness of one's ignorance.
author: Anthony De Mello

text: One does what one is; one becomes what one does.
author: Robert Musil

text: Every book we read must leave us richer or poorer, sadder or happier, safer or more uncertain, but never intact.
author: Nicolás Gómez Dávila

text: If we are ever in doubt what to do, it is a good rule to ask ourselves what we shall wish on the morrow that we had done.
author: John Lubbock

text: Anxiety's like a rocking chair. It gives you something to do, but it doesn't get you very far.
author: Jodi Picoult

text: I had the epiphany that laughter was light, and light was laughter, and that this was the secret of the universe.
author: Donna Tartt

text:
One of my favorite lessons I’ve learnt from working with smart people:

Action produces information. If you’re unsure of what to do, just do anything, even if it’s the wrong thing. This will give you information about what you should actually be doing.

Sounds simple on the surface - the hard part is making it part of your every day working process.
author: Brian Armstrong

text: If you are patient in one moment of anger, you will escape 100 days of sorrow.
author: Chinese proverb

text: When I argue with reality, I lose, but only 100% of the time.
author: Byron Katie

text: I am not a product of my circumstances. I am a product of my decisions.
author: Stephen Covey

text: The art of life is to know how to enjoy a little and to endure very much.
author: William Hazlitt

text: Only a burning patience will lead to the attainment of a splendid happiness.
author: Pablo Neruda

text: As something, I am merely that thing. As no-thing, I am all things.
author: Douglas Harding

text: Children must be taught how to think, not what to think.
author: Margaret Mead

text: Be able to be alone. Lose not the advantage of solitude, and the society of thyself.
author: Thomas Browne

text: You shouldn’t worry about criticism from someone that you would never ask advice from.
author: Brian Halligan

text: What got you here won't get you there.
author: Marshall Goldsmith

text: One of my hopes is to age into a better mindset. The general trend seems to become less open minded, less resilient, less capable of handling change with ease and flexibility as the years roll by. I hope to grow in the opposite direction. How can my mindset be better today than it was yesterday?
author: James Clear

text: Words define us, they explain us, and, on occasion, they serve to control or isolate us.
author: Pip Williams

text: Humans are not ideally set up to understand logic; they are ideally set up to understand stories.
author: Roger Schank
